target.title: fix(ui): keep clampText/truncateText surrogate-safe at emoji boundaries
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`clampText` and `truncateText` in `ui/src/lib/format.ts` used `String.prototype.slice(0, N)` to truncate user-visible text. When the truncation boundary falls inside a UTF-16 surrogate pair (emoji like 🎉, CJK extended characters), the resulting string contains a dangling surrogate that browsers render as U+FFFD (�).

**Affected UI surfaces (all via `clampText` / `truncateText` calls):**

| Surface | File | Impact |
|---------|------|--------|
| Markdown rendering | `ui/src/components/markdown.ts` (3 sites) | User-written markdown with emoji truncates to � |
| Command autocomplete | `ui/src/lib/chat/commands.ts` (5 sites) | Command names/descriptions with emoji show broken chars |
| Tool output preview | `ui/src/pages/chat/tool-stream.ts` | Streamed tool output truncated mid-emoji |
| Activity log preview | `ui/src/pages/activity/tool-activity.ts` | Activity feed entries with emoji show corruption |
| Skill descriptions | `ui/src/pages/skills/view.ts` (2 sites) | Skill summary/description truncated at emoji |
| Exec-approval rules | `ui/src/pages/nodes/view-exec-approvals.ts` (3 sites) | Approval rule descriptions, commands, paths with emoji |

## Changes

**`ui/src/lib/format.ts`** (+2, −2):
- Import `truncateUtf16Safe` from `@openclaw/normalization-core/utf16-slice`
- `clampText()`: `value.slice(0, max-1)` → `truncateUtf16Safe(value, max-1)`
- `truncateText()`: `value.slice(0, max)` → `truncateUtf16Safe(value, max)`

**`ui/src/lib/format.test.ts`** (+82):
- Add `clampText` and `truncateText` to imports
- Add `clampText surrogate-safe truncation` test suite (3 tests)
- Add `truncateText surrogate-safe truncation` test suite (3 tests)
- Each suite verifies truncation at an emoji boundary produces no dangling surrogates using `isHighSurrogate`/`isLowSurrogate` checks

## Evidence

**Unit tests (43/45 passed — 2 pre-existing locale failures unrelated to change):**

```
 Test Files  1 failed (1)  ← pre-existing locale issue
      Tests  2 failed | 43 passed (45)
```

The 2 failed tests (`forces a 12-hour clock when preference is 12`, `lets the caller override the resolved hour cycle`) are pre-existing locale-sensitive tests that expect `/PM/i` but receive Chinese‑locale output `下午07:30`. All 6 new truncation tests pass.

**Real behavior proof (platinum):**

```
[+0.001s][LIN-66D8BD4EA2C:3099698] ═══ Platinum Proof: format.ts surrogate-safe truncation ═══
[+0.001s][LIN-66D8BD4EA2C:3099698]
[+0.001s][LIN-66D8BD4EA2C:3099698] Text: 118 a + 🎉(2 units) + b = 121 UTF-16 units
[+0.001s][LIN-66D8BD4EA2C:3099698] [BEFORE] .slice(0, 119): lone surrogate? ✗ BROKEN
[+0.001s][LIN-66D8BD4EA2C:3099698] [AFTER]  sliceUtf16Safe(0, 119): lone surrogate? ✓ OK
[+0.001s][LIN-66D8BD4EA2C:3099698] clampText(..., 120): lone surrogate? ✓ OK
[+0.001s][LIN-66D8BD4EA2C:3099698] truncateText(..., 120): lone surrogate? ✓ OK

[+0.001s][LIN-66D8BD4EA2C:3099698]   🐚 RESULT: PASS (platinum)
[+0.001s][LIN-66D8BD4EA2C:3099698]   Unsafe .slice() produces dangling surrogates at emoji boundary.
[+0.001s][LIN-66D8BD4EA2C:3099698]   truncateUtf16Safe (and clampText/truncateText) eliminate them.
```

*Proof method: spawned a real Node.js process importing the fixed functions, tested truncation with emoji 🎉 positioned exactly at the boundary. Unsafe `.slice()` produces dangling surrogates; `truncateUtf16Safe`, `clampText`, and `truncateText` all produce clean output.*

## Review
- Manually reviewed and verified
- AI-assisted: Yes
